body:
## Problem

Every remote git operation takes a per-repository lock around the shared bare mirror. `GitRef.tree` held that lock for the **entire** checkout: copying objects, checking out files, cloning submodules over the network, and normalizing timestamps.

Only the first step touches the mirror. The rest operate on the caller's private checkout directory, but they still held the lock. So a repository with a slow submodule serialized everything else on that repository behind it:

- `GitRef.log`, `GitCommit` metadata reads, and `GitRepository.remote` waited for a submodule clone they had nothing to do with.
- Two `tree` calls on different refs of the same repository ran strictly one after the other, including their submodule clones and file checkouts.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as tree(main)
    participant L as mirror lock
    participant M as mirror (shared)
    participant C as checkout A (private)
    participant B as log(main)

    A->>L: lock
    A->>M: fetch missing objects
    M->>C: git fetch file://mirror
    B->>L: lock (blocked)
    A->>C: git checkout
    A->>C: git submodule update (network, slow)
    A->>C: normalize timestamps
    A->>L: unlock
    B->>L: lock
    B->>M: git log
```

## Change

Split the checkout into the phase that needs the mirror and the phase that does not, and release the mirror between them.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as tree(main)
    participant L as mirror lock
    participant M as mirror (shared)
    participant C as checkout A (private)
    participant B as log(main)

    A->>L: lock
    A->>M: fetch missing objects
    M->>C: git fetch file://mirror
    A->>L: unlock
    par checkout continues unlocked
        A->>C: git checkout
        A->>C: git submodule update (network, slow)
        A->>C: normalize timestamps
    and unrelated reads proceed
        B->>L: lock
        B->>M: git log
        B->>L: unlock
    end
```

**This does not introduce concurrent access to the mirror.** The mirror is still only read or written under the lock, exactly as before. What runs outside the lock only touches the checkout's own `.git` and worktree, which no other caller can see, plus the network for submodules. `git fetch` from a `file://` URL goes through the pack transport, so the checkout owns full copies of its objects: no alternates, no hardlinks, no reference back to the mirror.

Concretely:

- `doGitCheckout` is split into `fetchGitCheckout` (init + fetch from the mirror) and `finishGitCheckout` (everything else). Local repositories still call the combined function; only the remote path releases the mirror between phases.
- `RemoteGitRef.Tree` mounts the checkout first, borrows the mirror only for `fetchGitCheckout`, then finishes with the mirror released.
- Credential and network setup (SSH agent socket, known hosts, resolv, auth headers) are set up in `Tree` so they outlive the mirror mount, since submodule clones still need them.
- Lock waits, mirror acquisition, and mirror mounting each get an internal span, so slow checkouts are diagnosable in traces.

Extracted from vitoland commit `0ef9bc2d36`, adapted to main's checkout signatures. No workspace Git API dependency.

## Tests

- `TestGitCheckoutIndependentAfterFetch` (unit) runs the fetch phase, **deletes the source repository**, then runs the finish phase and `git fsck --full`. Covers full history, shallow, and discarded git dir. This is the guarantee that nothing after the unlock can reach the mirror.
- `TestGitLogDuringCheckout` (integration) gates the submodule's pack transfer on the server side and requires a concurrent `log` on the same repository to complete while the checkout is stuck. It fails on main.

Validation through `engine-dev test`: unit test passed with the race detector ([trace](https://dagger.cloud/dagger/traces/f7691b7a868d01e8ad3b41867092685b)); the integration regression passed ([trace](https://dagger.cloud/dagger/traces/250e7a6fd72d046d4f516b8dcfad41da)).
title: fix(git): release mirrors before checkout
